Jeremiyah Love: Notre Dame RB drafted No. 3 overall by the Arizona Cardinals in the 2026 NFL Draft, the highest RB selection since Saquon Barkley. Love piled up 40 TDs over his last two college seasons and signed a four-year, $53M deal with the most guaranteed money ever for a RB. He projects as an immediate three-down starter and is the consensus 1.01 in dynasty rookie drafts, with Mike LaFleur's scheme being called a 'seamless' fit after May 8-10 rookie minicamp.
Fernando Mendoza: Indiana QB taken No. 1 overall by the Las Vegas Raiders in the 2026 NFL Draft after winning the Heisman and leading the Hoosiers to a 16-0 national title. Led FBS with 41 passing TDs on a 72% completion rate. He joins Burrow and Cam Newton as the only QBs to win the Heisman, a national title, and go No. 1 overall in consecutive years. Locked-in Week 1 starter in Vegas and a top-tier dynasty superflex asset.
Carnell Tate: Ohio State WR drafted No. 4 overall by the Tennessee Titans, the first WR off the board in 2026. Titans GM Mike Borgonzi called him 'the best receiver in the draft.' He posted 51-875-9 in his junior year despite missing three games to injury, earning second-team All-American honors. Pairs with rookie QB Cam Ward as the alpha X-receiver in Tennessee and is a top-3 dynasty rookie WR with WR1 upside.
Makai Lemon: USC WR taken No. 20 overall by the Philadelphia Eagles, who traded up from No. 23 to grab him ahead of the Steelers. The 2025 Biletnikoff winner posted 79-1,156-11 last season as a compact, twitchy slot with elite YAC ability. Slots into a crowded Eagles WR room behind A.J. Brown and DeVonta Smith, which caps his Year 1 ceiling but his route-running profile gives him real long-term dynasty upside as the eventual heir.
Jordyn Tyson: Arizona State WR selected No. 8 overall by the New Orleans Saints, highest ASU draft pick since 1976. The 6-2, 203 prospect had 158-2,282-22 career receiving, including a 1,101-yard breakout in 2024. He drew rave reviews from Day 1 of Saints rookie minicamp on May 8 lining up at three spots, signed a four-year $32.5M deal, and sat out Day 2 for routine 'maintenance' (not injury). Profiles as the Saints' immediate WR1 with elite dynasty stock.
Kenyon Sadiq: Oregon TE drafted No. 16 overall by the New York Jets, the top TE off the board in 2026. Set an Oregon single-season TE record (51-560-8 TDs, FBS lead) and ran a 4.39 forty at the combine, fastest by any TE in 20+ years. Signed his rookie deal in early May. Lands in a tight end-needy Jets offense with new HC Aaron Glenn and has clear path to immediate target volume, making him the dynasty TE1 rookie with TE1 overall ceiling.
Arvell Reese: Ohio State LB taken No. 5 overall by the New York Giants, the first pick of the John Harbaugh era. The 6-4, 243 hybrid LB/edge logged 69 tackles (10 TFL), 6.5 sacks and earned first-team All-American and Big Ten Linebacker of the Year. Used as a moveable chess piece in college and projects as a Day 1 every-down starter. Top-tier dynasty IDP LB1 with sack and tackle equity baked into his hybrid usage.
Sonny Styles: Ohio State LB selected No. 7 overall by the Washington Commanders, making OSU the first school ever with two LBs taken in the top 10 of the same draft. The 6-5, 244 former safety posted 100 tackles, 10.5 TFL, six sacks in 2024 and put up a 4.46 forty with a 43.5-inch vertical (best ever for an LB at the combine). Plug-and-play starter in Dan Quinn's defense and an elite IDP LB1 with rare athletic upside.
KC Concepcion: Texas A&M WR drafted No. 24 overall by the Cleveland Browns. The Paul Hornung Award winner (most versatile player in CFB) posted 61-919-9 at A&M after transferring from NC State. Joins a Browns offense that took Shedeur Sanders to be the new starter, which gives him real target volume in a thin Cleveland WR room. A polished slot/gadget weapon with PPR-friendly usage, he's a back-end dynasty rookie WR1/WR2 with quicker fantasy ascent than most Day 1 receivers.
Omar Cooper: Indiana WR taken No. 30 overall by the New York Jets after they traded up from No. 33. The 6-0, 199 receiver was Fernando Mendoza's top target during Indiana's 16-0 title run, posting 69-937-13 (his 13 TDs tied for third in FBS). Reunites with WR-friendly OC Tanner Engstrand on a Jets offense looking for a true X opposite Garrett Wilson. Solid dynasty rookie WR2 with red-zone upside if he wins early reps.
Caleb Downs: Ohio State safety drafted No. 11 overall by the Dallas Cowboys, who traded up from No. 12 to get him. Two-time unanimous All-American and the 2025 Jim Thorpe Award winner, he's considered a generational safety prospect (his model score trails only Derwin James and Minkah Fitzpatrick since 2018). Plug-and-play starter in Dallas's safety-friendly scheme. The clear DB1 of the class and a top-5 IDP rookie pick overall with elite long-term tackle and playmaking upside.
David Bailey: Texas Tech edge rusher taken No. 2 overall by the New York Jets, the highest pick of the Jets' three first-rounders in 2026. After three years at Stanford, Bailey transferred and exploded for 14.5 sacks, 19.5 TFL and 81 pressures as a unanimous All-American and Big 12 Defensive Lineman of the Year. Ran 4.50 at the combine. Considered the best pure pass rusher in the class and a Day 1 starting edge for Aaron Glenn, making him a top-3 IDP DL rookie with double-digit sack upside as a rookie.
Jacob Rodriguez: Texas Tech LB who went No. 43 overall (2nd round) to the Miami Dolphins in the 2026 NFL Draft. A converted QB-turned-linebacker, Rodriguez swept the 2025 Butkus, Nagurski, Bednarik and Lombardi awards after posting 128 tackles, 11 TFLs, 7 forced fumbles and 4 INTs. He sits behind starters Jordyn Brooks and Tyrel Dodson in 2026, but both are pending free agents, giving him a clear path to a three-down role by 2027. Premier IDP dynasty stash with elite tackle production upside.
Denzel Boston: Washington WR drafted No. 39 overall (2nd round) by the Cleveland Browns, joining 1st-round WR KC Concepcion in a revamped pass-catcher room. The 6'3", 213-pound contested-catch specialist led the Huskies with 11 TDs and 881 yards in 2025. Projected to start opposite Jerry Jeudy and Concepcion under HC Todd Monken. Dynasty profile is a low-end WR3 with red-zone upside, though his lack of separation speed and the Browns' shaky QB situation cap his immediate ceiling.
Eli Stowers: Vanderbilt TE selected No. 54 overall (2nd round) by the Philadelphia Eagles. The 2025 Mackey Award winner and Campbell Trophy recipient is a QB-turned-TE who set Combine TE records in broad jump (11'3") and vertical (45.5"). He sits behind Dallas Goedert, who is on a one-year deal, so dynasty managers should view Stowers as the Eagles' TE of the future starting in 2027. Limited 2026 fantasy ceiling unless Goedert misses time, but elite long-term dynasty TE2 value.
Jadarian Price: Notre Dame RB taken No. 32 overall (final pick of Round 1) by the Seattle Seahawks, replacing departed Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III. Never started a college game but averaged 6.0 YPC with 21 TDs and was a first-team All-American kick returner. With Zach Charbonnet out long-term after a January ACL tear, Price is the projected Week 1 starter and is in line for 15-plus touches per game. Top-tier 2026 rookie RB value in dynasty with immediate workload.
Dillon Thieneman: Oregon S taken No. 25 overall (1st round) by the Chicago Bears, the highest-drafted Oregon safety in school history. A consensus All-American in 2025 with 99 tackles, 2 INTs and a 4.35 40, Thieneman locks in as a Day 1 starter alongside Coby Bryant. Elite tackle production (97th-percentile tackle rate) makes him a high-floor IDP rookie — ranked behind only Caleb Downs at safety in most rookie IDP rankings. Plug-and-play DB1 in deep IDP dynasty leagues.
Jake Golday: Cincinnati LB selected No. 51 overall (2nd round) by the Minnesota Vikings. At 6'4"/239 with a 9.85 RAS, the First-Team All-Big 12 pick logged 105 tackles, 3.5 sacks and a 39-inch vert in 2025. Likely opens as the SAM/sub-package LB in Brian Flores' defense behind Blake Cashman (UFA after 2026), pointing to a full-time role by 2027. Solid mid-round IDP rookie pick with three-down upside thanks to his blitz and coverage range.
CJ Allen: Georgia LB drafted No. 53 overall (2nd round) by the Indianapolis Colts. The 6'1"/230-pound former Bulldogs captain led Georgia with 88 tackles, 8 TFLs and 3.5 sacks in 2025. With Zaire Franklin traded to Green Bay in March, Allen has a clear path to take over the MIKE role and the defensive signal-calling duties. Elite run-defender profile with potential to be a top-15 IDP LB in volume terms; coverage limitations are the main concern. Strong Year 1 IDP starter.
Ty Simpson: Alabama QB and surprise No. 13 overall (1st round) selection by the Los Angeles Rams. The 23-year-old finished 2025 with a 28:5 TD-to-INT ratio and 64.5% completions, earning Second-Team All-SEC honors and Heisman buzz before fading down the stretch. He'll redshirt behind reigning MVP Matthew Stafford in 2026 while learning Sean McVay's offense, with a clear runway to the starting job in 2027. Long-term superflex/dynasty QB asset with elite landing-spot value.
Rueben Bain: Miami EDGE picked No. 15 overall (1st round) by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The 2025 ACC Defensive Player of the Year and Ted Hendricks Award winner had 9.5 sacks and led all draft EDGEs in QB hurries his final two seasons. Slight size concerns (sub-31-inch arms, ~265 lbs) caused a small slide, but he's the favorite for 2026 Defensive Rookie of the Year and is projected as an immediate starter with weekly IDP spike-week upside. Mid-to-late 2nd-round rookie pick in IDP dynasty.
Jonah Coleman: Washington RB taken No. 108 overall (4th round) by the Denver Broncos. The compact, physical runner had 15 rushing TDs in 2025 and only one career fumble on 552 college touches — elite ball security. Currently the RB3 behind J.K. Dobbins and 2025 second-rounder RJ Harvey, but Dobbins' injury history and Coleman's goal-line skill set give him real handcuff appeal in Sean Payton's offense. Late-round dynasty flier with a clear path to relevance if injuries hit.
Elijah Sarratt: Indiana WR drafted No. 115 overall (4th round) by the Baltimore Ravens. The 6'2"/207-pound possession receiver led the nation with 15 TDs in 2025 and finished his career with 44 TDs across three programs. Slots into a crowded depth chart behind Zay Flowers, Rashod Bateman, Devontez Walker and 3rd-rounder Ja'Kobi Lane. Limited 2026 fantasy ceiling but his contested-catch ability and Lamar Jackson connection make him a worthwhile late-round dynasty stash.
Nicholas Singleton: Penn State RB taken No. 165 overall (5th round) by the Tennessee Titans. Penn State's all-time leader in all-purpose yards (5,586) and total TDs (55), Singleton missed the entire pre-draft process recovering from January foot surgery suffered during Senior Bowl week. Joins a backfield with Tony Pollard, Tyjae Spears and Michael Carter — all UFAs after 2026, meaning Singleton is the only RB under contract for 2027. Sneaky-value dynasty pick with a likely path to a Year 2 lead role under a new coaching staff.
Mike Washington: RB drafted by the Las Vegas Raiders in the fourth round (No. 122) of the 2026 NFL Draft out of Arkansas, where he ran for 1,070 yards and 8 TDs as a transfer in 2025. The 6-1, 223-pound back lit up the combine with a class-best 4.33 40 but slid in the draft due to fumbling concerns. He lands behind first-rounder Ashton Jeanty in Vegas, so dynasty value is muted: change-of-pace/handcuff with upside if Jeanty gets hurt, but a clear backup otherwise.
Chris Brazzell: WR taken by the Carolina Panthers in the third round (No. 83) of the 2026 NFL Draft after a breakout senior year at Tennessee (62-1,017-9, led the SEC in receiving yards). The 6-4, 198-pound burner ran a 4.37 with an 80+ inch wingspan, profiling as a vertical Z with a Christian Watson-style comp. Joins a thin Panthers WR room as an outside complement to Xavier Legette and could carve out a real role quickly, making him a solid mid-round dynasty rookie target with deep-ball upside.
Emmett Johnson: RB selected by the Kansas City Chiefs in the fifth round (No. 161) of the 2026 NFL Draft after a 1,451-yard, 12-TD rushing season at Nebraska that earned him Big Ten RB of the Year honors. The 5-11, 200-pound junior also caught 46 balls for 370 yards, showing the three-down skill set Andy Reid loves. Buried behind Isiah Pacheco for now, but as a Day 3 receiving back in this offense he has sneaky stash appeal in dynasty PPR formats.
Garrett Nussmeier: QB dropped to the Kansas City Chiefs in the seventh round (No. 249) of the 2026 NFL Draft after his stock collapsed from a preseason projected No. 1 overall pick. The former LSU starter battled a nerve-cyst in his torso that sapped his arm strength, finishing 2025 with just 1,927 yards and 12 TDs in 9 games. As Patrick Mahomes' new backup, his dynasty value is essentially zero in 1QB leagues; SuperFlex deep stash only with hopes a healthy offseason restores some upside.
Chris Bell: WR drafted by the Miami Dolphins in the third round (No. 94) of the 2026 NFL Draft out of Louisville, where he posted career-bests of 72-917-6 and earned First-Team All-ACC and Biletnikoff Award semifinalist honors. The 6-2, 220-pound big-bodied receiver gives Miami a contested-catch X to complement Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle. Path to immediate volume is limited behind those two, but he is a strong dynasty WR3/4 with red-zone upside and a clear runway if either star moves on.
Josiah Trotter: LB taken by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the second round (No. 46) of the 2026 NFL Draft out of Missouri (transfer from West Virginia), where he was a First-Team All-SEC pick. The son of former NFL LB Jeremiah Trotter and brother of Jeremiah Jr., he brings a 176-tackle, 17-TFL college resume and instinctive downhill play. Slots in next to Lavonte David and projects as a Day 1 starter alongside (or eventual replacement for) the veteran, making him a top-tier IDP rookie LB target.
Emmanuel McNeil-Warren: Safety drafted by the Cleveland Browns in the second round (No. 58) of the 2026 NFL Draft out of Toledo, where he produced 77 tackles, 5.5 TFLs, 2 INTs and 3 forced fumbles as a senior. Many boards had him as a top-25 prospect, so the Browns landed a value. Joins a Cleveland safety room where he should see early snaps near the line of scrimmage, giving him strong IDP upside as a tackle-producing rookie box safety and one of the better under-the-radar dynasty IDP picks in the class.
A.J. Haulcy: Safety taken by the Indianapolis Colts in the third round (No. 78) of the 2026 NFL Draft, capping a journey through New Mexico, Houston and LSU. The 6-0, 215-pound strong safety earned First-Team All-SEC honors in 2025 and finished his career with 10 picks. A smart, instinctive box defender rather than a coverage athlete, he fits well in Indy's defense and has a chance to compete for early snaps, making him a solid mid-round IDP rookie safety with tackle volume upside.
Zachariah Branch: WR selected by the Atlanta Falcons in the third round (No. 79) of the 2026 NFL Draft out of Georgia (transfer from USC). The former five-star recruit caught 81-811-6 to lead the Bulldogs in 2025 and ran a 4.35 at the combine. Small-framed at ~180 lbs but elite with the ball in space, he projects as the Falcons' slot/gadget weapon behind Drake London and Darnell Mooney. Boom-bust dynasty WR3/4 with PPR appeal and elite return-game floor.
Anthony Hill: LB drafted by the Tennessee Titans in the second round (No. 60) of the 2026 NFL Draft as the first Longhorn off the board. The 6-2, 238-pound, two-time second-team All-SEC defender finished his Texas career with 249 tackles, 17 sacks, 31.5 TFLs and 8 forced fumbles. A three-down hybrid who can rush off the edge or play off-ball, he should step into immediate snaps in Tennessee and is one of the top IDP rookie LBs in the class with both tackle and big-play upside.
Malachi Lawrence: EDGE selected by the Dallas Cowboys at No. 23 overall in the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft after Dallas traded down with Philadelphia. The 6-4, 253-pound UCF rusher logged 7 sacks, 11 TFLs and First-Team All-Big 12 honors in 2025, then turned heads at the combine with a 4.52 40, 40-inch vertical and 10-10 broad. First-round capital plus reuniting with his former UCF coach in Dallas gives him a clear path to early snaps and elite IDP DL upside as a dynasty rookie.
R Mason Thomas: EDGE drafted by the Kansas City Chiefs in the second round (No. 40) of the 2026 NFL Draft out of Oklahoma, where he earned First-Team All-SEC honors despite missing three games with a quad injury (26 tackles, 9.5 TFLs, 6.5 sacks). At 6-2, 241 lbs with a 4.67 40, he is undersized but a polished, twitched-up speed-to-power rusher. Likely a third-down sub-package piece early in Steve Spagnuolo's scheme, making him a mid-tier dynasty IDP rookie pass-rusher with situational sack upside.
T.J. Parker: EDGE, Clemson. Selected by the Buffalo Bills with the No. 35 overall pick (Round 2) in the 2026 NFL Draft. Parker leaves Clemson after a productive three-year run with 21.5 sacks, 41.5 TFLs, and six forced fumbles, slotting in behind Greg Rousseau and A.J. Epenesa on Buffalo's edge depth chart with a clear path to a rotational/sub-package role as a rookie. Dynasty IDP managers should view him as a high-floor, fast-track pass rusher who could push for double-digit pressures in Year 1 with growing snap share.
Cashius Howell: EDGE, Texas A&M. Cincinnati grabbed him at No. 41 overall in Round 2 of the 2026 NFL Draft after a Unanimous All-American, SEC Defensive Player of the Year season featuring 11.5 sacks. At 6'2/253 with notably short 30.3-inch arms (shortest by an EDGE since 1999, which slid him out of Round 1), he projects as a rotational rusher behind Boye Mafe and across from Shemar Stewart on Al Golden's revamped front. Solid dynasty IDP buy with sack upside, though length concerns cap his ceiling.
Keldric Faulk: EDGE/DL, Auburn. Tennessee took him 31st overall in Round 1 of the 2026 NFL Draft. At 6'6, 275 pounds and just 20 years old, Faulk brings elite strength (700-pound squat) and led FBS edge defenders in run stops over three seasons. Third-team All-SEC in 2025, he's a long-term IDP cornerstone for the Titans with positional versatility to play inside or outside. Expect immediate run-defense snaps with pass-rush production growing into Year 2-3 — strong dynasty rookie hold.
Akheem Mesidor: EDGE, Miami. Selected by the Los Angeles Chargers at No. 22 overall in Round 1 of the 2026 NFL Draft. The 25-year-old Canadian had a breakout 2025 under Jason Taylor — 12.5 sacks, 17.5 TFLs, four forced fumbles, First-Team All-ACC. He lands in a dream IDP spot opposite Khalil Mack on Jesse Minter's defense, where rotational reps and sub-package work should produce solid Year 1 numbers. Age is the only knock; dynasty managers should treat him as a 2-3 year window asset with high floor.
Kaytron Allen: RB, Penn State. Washington took him in Round 6 (No. 187 overall) of the 2026 NFL Draft. Penn State's all-time leading rusher (4,180 yards, 39 TDs) lacks elite burst but is a physical, elusive grinder who could quickly carve out a short-yardage and goal-line role behind a messy Commanders committee of Rachaad White, Jerome Ford, and Jacory Croskey-Merritt. Late-round dynasty dart throw with legitimate path to early touches — some analysts have even floated him as a sneaky RB1 candidate by midseason.
Malachi Fields: WR, Notre Dame (via Virginia). Selected by the New York Giants at No. 74 overall in Round 3 of the 2026 NFL Draft. The 6'4, 218-pound X-receiver ran 4.61 and fits the prototypical big-bodied boundary mold. He steps into a Giants WR room that should give him a clear path to early targets opposite Malik Nabers. Dynasty managers get an immediate WR3 with upside as a contested-catch, red-zone weapon — a strong rookie pick in the late second/early third of rookie drafts.
Trinidad Chambliss: QB, Ole Miss. Chambliss did NOT enter the 2026 NFL Draft — the former Ferris State transfer chose to return to Oxford for another year of starting after the NCAA denied his waiver appeal initially, then his situation resolved in his favor. In 2025 he threw for 3,937 yards and 22 TDs (3 INTs) with 527 rushing yards and eight scores, earning SEC Newcomer of the Year while leading Ole Miss to the CFP semis. He'll be a top-tier 2027 QB prospect with Round 1-2 buzz.
Germie Bernard: WR, Alabama. Pittsburgh traded up to grab him at No. 47 overall in Round 2 of the 2026 NFL Draft. Bernard led the Tide with 64 catches for 862 yards and 7 TDs in 2025 and is one of the more polished route runners in the class. Mike McCarthy raved about him at rookie minicamp ('Football comes easy to him'), and he's already building chemistry with Drew Allar. With only DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr. ahead of him, Bernard has a wide-open path to the WR3 role — strong dynasty rookie target.
Max Klare: TE, Ohio State (via Purdue). Selected by the Los Angeles Rams at No. 61 overall in Round 2 of the 2026 NFL Draft. The 6'4, 246-pound Klare caught 43-448-2 in 2025 and joins a deep room with Colby Parkinson, Tyler Higbee, Terrance Ferguson, and Davis Allen ahead of him. However, the Rams ran their 13 personnel package on 30.5% of snaps last year (NFL-high), and ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reports L.A. expects him to contribute. Solid dynasty TE2 with pass-game upside who could climb quickly.
Ja'Kobi Lane: WR, USC. Baltimore took him at No. 80 overall in Round 3 of the 2026 NFL Draft. At 6'4, 208 pounds with a 40-inch vertical and the biggest hands (10.5") of any WR in the class, Lane is a prototypical X with elite ball skills (18 career TDs at USC). He already flashed at Ravens rookie minicamp with a highlight crosser grab. Lands in a great spot catching from Lamar Jackson with a clear long-term WR2 trajectory behind Zay Flowers — buy-now dynasty asset with Year 1 red-zone upside.
Michael Trigg: TE, Baylor (via USC, Ole Miss). Trigg WENT UNDRAFTED in the 2026 NFL Draft and signed with the Dallas Cowboys as a UDFA. The 6'4, 240-pound athletic move TE had a career year at Baylor — 50-694-6, Mackey Award finalist, First-Team All-Big 12, AP third-team All-American — with comps to Evan Engram and Isaiah Likely. Blocking limitations and a journeyman path hurt his stock. Deep dynasty taxi-squad flier only; needs to win a roster spot in Dallas behind Jake Ferguson before he's startable.
Skyler Bell: WR, UConn (via Wisconsin). Buffalo selected him at No. 125 overall in Round 4 of the 2026 NFL Draft. The Bronx native turned down a reported $500K Michigan NIL offer to stay at UConn and posted 101-1,278-13 in 2025 as a Biletnikoff finalist and consensus All-American. He ran 4.40 with a 41-inch vertical and projects as a twitchy slot/movement piece. Bell's arrival has put incumbent Bills WRs in roster trouble, giving him a real Year 1 path to snaps — interesting late-round dynasty dart in a Josh Allen offense.
Keionte Scott: Slot cornerback drafted by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the 4th round (No. 116) of the 2026 NFL Draft after a strong final season at Miami (Auburn and Houston transfer). The 24-year-old projects as a high-floor nickel with strong blitzing chops and run-game thump (13 TFL, 5 sacks at Miami in 2025), giving him IDP appeal in tackle-heavy leagues. Recent news of a wrist surgery is worth monitoring, but he should compete for early sub-package snaps in Todd Bowles' aggressive defense.
Antonio Williams: Slot wide receiver selected by the Washington Commanders in the 3rd round (No. 71) of the 2026 NFL Draft out of Clemson. The 6'0", 195-pound Third-Team All-ACC product led the Tigers with 55 catches for 604 yards and 4 TDs as a senior and finished his career with 207 receptions for 2,320 yards and 21 scores. He profiles as a smooth route-running slot with speed and YAC ability, making him a quality dynasty stash behind Terry McLaurin in a developing Commanders offense.
Derrick Moore: Edge rusher taken by the Detroit Lions in the 2nd round (No. 44) of the 2026 NFL Draft after the team traded up from No. 50. The Michigan product capped his college career with 10.5 TFL and 10 sacks in 2025 and is viewed as one of the most pro-ready edge rushers in the class thanks to violent hands, technique, and motor. He'll compete with DJ Wonnum opposite Aidan Hutchinson for early rotational snaps, giving him strong dynasty IDP upside in a defense that generates pressure.
Jakobe Thomas: Ball-hawking safety selected by the Minnesota Vikings in the 3rd round (No. 98) of the 2026 NFL Draft. The 6'1", 211-pound Miami transfer (Middle Tennessee, Tennessee) posted a monster 2025 with 76 tackles, 5 INTs (one TD), 3.5 sacks and two forced fumbles for the CFP runner-up Hurricanes. His blend of size, range, and playmaking gives him plug-and-play IDP appeal in dynasty, and he has a path to early starting reps in Brian Flores's aggressive defense.
Zion Young: Edge defender drafted by the Baltimore Ravens in the 2nd round (No. 45) of the 2026 NFL Draft. The 6'5", 262-pound Missouri transfer (Michigan State) earned First-Team All-SEC after racking up 16.5 TFL, 6.5 sacks and 52 pressures in 2025. He pairs power and disruption as a pass rusher and stout run defender, giving the Ravens a long-term edge complement. Expect a rotational year one with dynasty IDP upside once he carves out a full-time role.
Jaishawn Barham: Hybrid linebacker/edge taken by the Dallas Cowboys in the 3rd round (No. 92) of the 2026 NFL Draft out of Michigan (Maryland transfer). After leading the Wolverines with 66 tackles as a junior off-ball linebacker, he moved to edge in 2025 and posted 10 TFL and 4 sacks. His positional versatility, downhill instincts, and developing pass-rush traits give him IDP intrigue, though his fantasy role will hinge on whether Dallas deploys him as a stack 'backer or a stand-up edge.
Bud Clark: Versatile safety selected by the Seattle Seahawks in the 2nd round (No. 64) of the 2026 NFL Draft out of TCU. The sixth-year senior finished his career with 214 tackles, 15 INTs and 35 PBUs, and ran a blazing 4.41 at the combine. He can range deep, match in the slot, and trigger in run support, making him an early candidate for sub-package snaps in Seattle's secondary. Sliding-frame concerns aside, the ball production is real and the dynasty IDP outlook is strong.
Keyron Crawford: Edge rusher taken by the Las Vegas Raiders in the 3rd round (No. 67) of the 2026 NFL Draft. The former basketball player (Arkansas State, then Auburn) is a raw but explosive athlete who earned Third-Team All-SEC honors in 2025 and finished his college career with 25 TFL and 11.5 sacks. With Maxx Crosby still anchoring the Raiders' edge group, Crawford has time to develop, but his physical tools and trajectory make him a worthwhile dynasty IDP stash with breakout upside.
Harold Perkins: Hybrid linebacker drafted by the Atlanta Falcons in the 6th round (No. 215) of the 2026 NFL Draft after a turbulent LSU career. Once viewed as a future top pick following 147 tackles, 13 sacks and 7 forced fumbles across his first two seasons, a torn ACL in 2024 derailed his stock. His 4.45 speed and Star-LB versatility fit Jeff Ulbrich's hybrid scheme, and the cost is right for a dynasty stash with elite athletic upside if he stays healthy.
Wade Woodaz: Coverage linebacker selected by the Houston Texans in the 4th round (No. 123) of the 2026 NFL Draft out of Clemson. The 6'3", 236-pound former safety converted to LB and finished his career with 201 tackles, 28.5 TFL and 9 sacks across 51 games while running 4.56. His length, range, and elite coverage ability give him a clear NFL niche on third downs and special teams, though he'll likely start as a rotational/STs piece behind Houston's veteran LB room.
Taurean York: Productive but undersized linebacker who went undrafted in the 2026 NFL Draft and reportedly signed with the Denver Broncos as a UDFA. The Texas A&M captain (5'10", 226) led the Aggies in tackles in both 2024 and 2025 and helped the team to its first CFP appearance. His instincts and production are legit, but 30-inch arms and a short frame torpedoed his draft stock. Dynasty-wise he's a deep-league flier who'll have to earn snaps via special teams.
Kyle Louis: Coverage linebacker/big-nickel hybrid taken by the Miami Dolphins in the 4th round (No. 138) of the 2026 NFL Draft out of Pittsburgh. The 6'0", 220-pound Senior Bowl standout (multiple INTs in 1-on-1s) finished his Pitt career with 201 tackles, 25.5 TFL, 10 sacks and 6 INTs. He fits the modern speed/space LB mold and should carve out a sub-package role quickly, giving him sneaky dynasty IDP appeal in big-play leagues despite the size questions.
Kevin Coleman: Slot WR out of Missouri (after stops at Jackson State, Louisville, and Mississippi State) drafted by the Miami Dolphins in the 5th round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Coleman led Mizzou with 66 catches for 732 yards in 2025 and projects as a developmental slot option behind Malik Washington. Dynasty value is modest — late-round rookie flier with a low ceiling unless injuries or depth-chart attrition open a path to targets in the third year of Tua Tagovailoa's offense.
Jack Endries: Texas TE selected by the Cincinnati Bengals at pick 221 (Round 7) in the 2026 NFL Draft after starting his career as a Cal walk-on. Endries posted a 3.1% drop rate and a 59% contested catch rate, profiling as a reliable receiving TE but with real run-blocking concerns (career 50.1 PFF block grade). Dynasty outlook is borderline TE2/low-end TE1 upside — a depth stash behind Mike Gesicki and Erick All who could carve out a role if injuries strike.
Demond Claiborne: Wake Forest RB taken by the Minnesota Vikings at pick 198 in the 2026 NFL Draft. The 5-10, 188-pound speedster ran a 4.37 forty and rushed for 907 yards in 2025 after a 1,049-yard 2024 season. Claiborne offers fluid change-of-direction, zone-scheme patience, and receiving chops, slotting in as a complement and potential change-of-pace behind Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason. Worth a mid-round dynasty rookie pick on speed and three-down skill set.
Ted Hurst: Georgia State WR (via Valdosta State) selected 84th overall by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Round 3 of the 2026 NFL Draft — the 15th receiver off the board. At 6-4, 210 with a 4.42 forty, Hurst posted a 1,000-yard senior season and was called one of The Athletic's 'favorite picks' of the entire draft. He projects as an outside/X receiver in Tampa behind Mike Evans and Emeka Egbuka with WR2/3 upside, making him a strong dynasty rookie target.
Cade Klubnik: Clemson QB drafted 110th overall (Round 4) by the New York Jets in 2026 after a disappointing senior season (66% completion, 16 TDs, 6 INTs). Klubnik joins a room with starter Geno Smith plus Brady Cook and Bailey Zappe, and the Jets are publicly committed to developing him slowly under Rich Reich's offense. Dynasty stash with SuperFlex relevance — if Geno falters mid-season, Klubnik could emerge as a fantasy option in 2026 or 2027.
Le'Veon Moss: Texas A&M RB who went undrafted in 2026 and signed with the Miami Dolphins as a UDFA after an ankle injury cut short his 2025 senior year (397 yards, 6 TDs in 7 games). The 2024 All-SEC Second Team back has a three-down skill set — pass-catching, pass-pro, and inside running — but lacks elite explosiveness and carries an injury history. Deep-roster dynasty flier only; he'll fight for the back end of Miami's RB depth chart behind De'Von Achane and Jaylen Wright.
J'Mari Taylor: Virginia RB (originally NC Central) who went undrafted in the 2026 NFL Draft and signed with the Jacksonville Jaguars as a UDFA. Taylor was projected as a mid-to-late round pick before sliding completely out of the draft, which damages his dynasty value significantly. He'll have to claw his way onto the roster behind Travis Etienne and Tank Bigsby in Jacksonville. Practice-squad-or-deep-bench dynasty stash only.
Jam Miller: Alabama RB selected by the New England Patriots at pick 245 (Round 7) of the 2026 NFL Draft. The 5-10, 209-pound back rushed for 1,596 yards and 13 TDs across 51 college games. Miller lands in a crowded Patriots backfield headed by Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson, so dynasty relevance hinges on injuries or special-teams contribution. Late-round dynasty flier with limited path to volume but decent build for short-yardage work.
Deion Burks: Oklahoma WR (via Purdue) taken 254th overall by the Indianapolis Colts in Round 7 of the 2026 NFL Draft. The 5-10, 180-pound speedster ran a 4.30 forty — fifth-fastest among WRs at the combine — and had one of the top overall combine performances at the position. Burks lands behind Alec Pierce and Josh Downs in a thin Colts WR room, giving him a real path to a WR3/slot role. Excellent late dynasty rookie target given the athleticism and opportunity.
Seth McGowan: Kentucky RB selected by the Indianapolis Colts at pick 237 (Round 7) of the 2026 NFL Draft. McGowan is a power back who 'falls forward' and wears down defenses between the tackles. He joins a Colts backfield led by Jonathan Taylor and will compete for a short-yardage/early-down change-of-pace role. Late-round dynasty handcuff value tied to Taylor's workload — limited standalone upside unless injuries open up touches.
CJ Daniels: Miami (FL) WR drafted 197th overall (Round 6) by the Los Angeles Rams in the 2026 NFL Draft, with LA trading picks 207, 251, and 252 to Philadelphia to move up for him. Daniels models his game after Davante Adams and is praised for elite hands and a polished route tree. The Rams' WR room (Puka Nacua, Davante Adams, Jordan Whittington) is crowded, but Daniels is a quality late dynasty rookie stash given his pedigree and Sean McVay's track record of developing receivers.
Justin Joly: Tight end out of NC State, drafted by the Denver Broncos in the 5th round (152nd overall) of the 2026 NFL Draft. The 6'3", 241-pound senior posted career-best 49 catches and 7 TDs in 2025, earning All-ACC honors. He brings strong hands and a wide catch radius as a red-zone target, but functional strength and blocking remain raw. Dynasty outlook is depth-piece TE2 with developmental upside behind Adam Trautman and Lucas Krull.
De'Zhaun Stribling: Wide receiver from Ole Miss (via Washington State and Oklahoma State), selected by the San Francisco 49ers with the 33rd overall pick (top of Round 2) in the 2026 NFL Draft. The 6'2", 207-pound burner ran a blazing 4.36 at the combine and posted 55-811-6 in his lone Ole Miss season. He projects as a vertical X-receiver with red-zone size in Kyle Shanahan's offense, giving him real Year 1 fantasy upside alongside Brandon Aiyuk and Ricky Pearsall.
Eli Raridon: 6'6", 245-pound Notre Dame tight end taken by the New England Patriots in the 3rd round (95th overall) of the 2026 NFL Draft. A senior season of 32-482 and a 36-inch combine vertical helped him stick despite a double ACL tear history from 2021-22. He pairs vertical speed with seam-stretching size and willing blocking, slotting in behind Hunter Henry as a developmental ascender in Drake Maye's offense. Solid late-round dynasty TE flier.
Oscar Delp: Georgia tight end taken by the New Orleans Saints at pick 73 (Round 3) of the 2026 NFL Draft. The 6'5", 245-pound four-year contributor blew up his pro day with a 4.49 40 and 38-inch vert, projecting as a three-down seam-busting TE. Career college numbers were modest (70-854-9 over four years), but his athletic profile and blocking versatility give him a runway in New Orleans behind a thin TE room. Mid-tier dynasty rookie TE2 with upside.
Carson Beck: Quarterback drafted by the Arizona Cardinals at pick 65 (Round 3) of the 2026 NFL Draft after his Miami transfer year (3,813 yards, 30-12 TD-INT) and a CFP title-game loss. The fourth QB off the board, Beck has prototype size, deep experience, and clean-pocket arm talent, but evaluators flagged inconsistent anticipation. He sits behind Kyler Murray as a developmental QB2 in Arizona; in superflex dynasty he's a back-end stash with bridge-starter ceiling.
Brenen Thompson: Wide receiver from Mississippi State (via Texas and Oklahoma) selected by the Los Angeles Chargers in the 4th round (105th overall) of the 2026 NFL Draft. The 5'9", 170-pound burner ran a 4.26 40 at the combine (third-fastest WR time ever) and broke Mississippi State's single-season receiving record with 57-1,054-6 in 2025. He projects as a field-stretching gadget/slot weapon for Justin Herbert, intriguing late-round dynasty dart with WR4 upside if his speed translates.
Drew Allar: Quarterback selected by the Pittsburgh Steelers in the 3rd round (76th overall) of the 2026 NFL Draft. The 6'5", 235-pound Penn State product flashed an NFL-caliber arm but never met the hype, and a season-ending ankle injury in October 2025 limited his final year to six games. Cast as a possible Aaron Rodgers heir, Allar lands in a soft developmental spot. Superflex dynasty has him as a QB3 stash with a clear path to start by 2027.
Kaelon Black: Running back from Indiana (not Texas A&M) drafted by the San Francisco 49ers in the 3rd round (90th overall) of the 2026 NFL Draft. The 5'10", 211-pound downhill back rushed for 1,034 yards and 10 TDs at 5.6 YPC under Curt Cignetti in 2025, earning elite PFF run grades. He projects as a power complement to Christian McCaffrey and a potential early-down/short-yardage hammer, making him a worthwhile dynasty handcuff with standalone value in PPR-light formats.
Zavion Thomas: Wide receiver from LSU (via Mississippi State) selected by the Chicago Bears in the 3rd round (89th overall) of the 2026 NFL Draft. The 5'10", 190-pound burner clocked 4.28 at the combine and was second-team All-SEC in 2025 (64-716-6) while serving as a high-volume return man. He offers slot/outside flex and special-teams value behind DJ Moore and Rome Odunze, with the speed to carve out a gadget role early. Late-round dynasty WR5 with upside.
Bryce Lance: North Dakota State wide receiver (brother of Trey Lance) taken by the New Orleans Saints in the 4th round (136th overall) of the 2026 NFL Draft. The 6'3", 204-pound first-team AP All-American averaged 21.2 yards per catch in 2025 and tested elite (4.34 40, 41.5" vert). He combines big-play ball skills with size mismatches but lacks elite release quickness. Lands on a thin Saints WR depth chart with a real path to snaps, giving him sneaky dynasty WR4 upside.
Sam Roush: Stanford tight end drafted by the Chicago Bears in the 3rd round (69th overall) of the 2026 NFL Draft. The massive 6'6", 267-pound senior led ACC TEs in receiving yards (49-545-2) and tested well at the combine (4.70 40, 38.5" vert). Best known as a high-end in-line blocker, he projects as Chicago's 13-personnel TE2 behind Colston Loveland and Cole Kmet. Limited fantasy ceiling but real-life role gives him touchdown-dependent flex value.
Eli Heidenreich: Navy RB/WR hybrid taken by the Pittsburgh Steelers in the 7th round (230th overall) of the 2026 NFL Draft. The 4.44 athlete finished as Navy's all-time receiving leader (1,994 yards) with 3,206 all-purpose yards and 23 TDs. He projects as a versatile depth weapon and gadget piece behind Jaylen Warren and Kaleb Johnson in Pittsburgh. Largely off the dynasty radar as a Day 3 service-academy hybrid; deep-roster taxi-squad flier only.
Caleb Douglas: Wide receiver from Texas Tech (via Florida) drafted by the Miami Dolphins in the 3rd round (75th overall) of the 2026 NFL Draft. The 6'4", 210-pound long-strider broke out in 2024 at Texas Tech (60-877-6) after an injury-shortened Florida tenure. He brings size, deep speed, and contested-catch upside that Tua Tagovailoa's offense can use opposite Tyreek Hill (or as Hill's successor if a trade happens). Solid mid-round dynasty WR with developmental WR3 ceiling.
Adam Randall: Clemson RB convert (former four-star WR) selected by the Baltimore Ravens in the 5th round (174th overall) of the 2026 NFL Draft. The 6'3", 232-pound bruiser rushed for 814 yards and 10 TDs as Clemson's starting back in 2025 after switching positions. Buried behind Derrick Henry, he projects as a Justice Hill replacement and pass-game complement long-term. Notable as the first pick owner Steve Bisciotti has ever made personally. Deep dynasty stash with Henry succession-plan intrigue.
Cole Payton: North Dakota State quarterback drafted by the Philadelphia Eagles in the 5th round (178th overall) of the 2026 NFL Draft, continuing NDSU's QB pipeline (Wentz, Stick, Lance, Miller). The 6'3", 232-pound lefty was a one-year starter who set NDSU records for passer rating (193.8) and YPA (12.1) while adding 777 rushing yards. Already being labeled the next Taysom Hill, Payton projects as a multi-positional weapon behind Jalen Hurts. Intriguing TE/QB-eligible dynasty dart in deep formats.
